people.name: Elon Musk
people.history: Co-founded Zip2 and X.com (later PayPal), then built Tesla and SpaceX. Bought Twitter in 2022 (now X) and founded xAI.

ecology.reason: Tesla’s electric cars cut tailpipe emissions; rockets and xAI data centres add energy use. Not assessed in detail.

politics.reason: Largest US political donor of 2024 ($291.5 million) and of the 2026 midterms (about $445 million). Led the DOGE cost-cutting effort in 2025, which targeted agencies holding contracts with his companies; those companies received at least $38 billion in public contracts, loans, subsidies and tax credits.

social.reason: Labour disputes at his companies and content moderation on X are widely reported; not yet sourced here.

legal.reason: Personal civil liability: a San Francisco jury found him liable in March 2026 for defrauding Twitter shareholders. Charged by the SEC with securities fraud in 2018 over Tesla tweets; settled a second SEC case in 2026 ($1.5 million) without admitting wrongdoing.

unresolved.reason: The January 2026 Epstein files include 2012–2013 emails in which he discussed visiting Epstein’s island, which contradicts his earlier statement that he refused. He says the emails are misinterpreted. No authority has accused him of a crime. Millions of identified pages remain unreleased.

people.counterweights: Tesla accelerated the shift to electric cars; SpaceX lowered launch costs.

ecology.label: Ecology
scale: Small physical footprint and no documented incident.
Indirect footprint: data centres, electronics, consumer goods, pharmaceuticals or finance.
Material footprint: mass retail, food, logistics platforms, cars, real estate or manufacturing.
Heavy footprint: mining, metals, cement, chemicals, shipping or fast fashion at global scale.
Fossil fuels as the core business, or a documented major environmental disaster.

politics.label: Politics
scale: No notable political activity found.
Ordinary corporate lobbying or occasional donations.
Major donor, owner of influential media, or documented political favours.
Among the largest donors of their country, or documented proximity to an authoritarian state.
Direct exercise of public power combined with top-scale election spending or platform control.

social.label: Social
scale: No concern found.
Ordinary sector-level concerns about labour, consumers or competition.
Documented company-level problems: labour findings, consumer settlements, market power.
Serious documented harm: court-established monopoly, forced or child labour findings, large health-harm settlements, arms or surveillance.
Deaths or mass harm documented in operations they control.

legal.label: Legal record
scale: No legal or regulatory record found.
Regulatory action, modest settlement or private disciplinary sanction.
Major company outcome: court finding, corporate plea, court administration or settlement above $1 billion.
Personal civil liability or penalty, personal sanctions, or a personal indictment even if later dropped.
Personal criminal conviction or guilty plea. A pardon or expungement is recorded, not erased.

unresolved.label: Open questions
scale: Nothing open found.
Opacity: private structures, little disclosure, or concerns raised only by reporting.
Pending case or investigation at company level.
Pending personal matter, or released documents raise unanswered questions about the person. Denials are recorded.
Several serious unresolved personal matters.
